note: One entry per trip round the CRISP-DM cycle. Findings go under the step where they were found. Never rewrite a closed iteration.

iterations.title: Quick, Draw! diamonds are mostly not rhombi
iterations.trigger: A modeling result on validation sent the project back to Data Preparation.
iterations.decision: All Quick, Draw! diamonds excluded by rule before the split; every model retrained.

findings.data: Review sheets showed most Quick, Draw! diamonds are gems, cones, shields or scribbles, which contradicts the class definition.
findings.prep: 500 drawings removed by rule. The split was re-frozen at 12,405 / 2,819 / 2,776.
findings.model: On validation, augmented models rejected those drawings (A1 recall 51 to 59%) while A0 memorized their style (86 to 93%).
findings.eval: Left in, this label noise would have penalized the arms that learn the real shape. Removed before any test read.

iterations.title: Augmentation lost to no augmentation
iterations.trigger: The Stage 5 verdict was fail, and A0, with no augmentation, scored highest. A validation-only investigation (16 trainings) found the cause, reported in docs/crisp_dm/iteration_2/investigation/report.md.
iterations.decision: Fix the transform defects, tune augmentation and generator on validation, add arm A2 (clean real + augmented real + synthetic), retrain and re-evaluate as a separately reported experiment, pre-registered in docs/crisp_dm/iteration_2/preregistration.md and scored on the reused test split and a fresh 4,500-image holdout. The iteration 1 verdict stands.

findings.business: The locked question was B vs A1. The result raises a different question: whether this augmentation design suits these classes at all. Iteration 2 answer: with the transform fixed and every arm tuned, the pre-registered A2 vs A0 test failed on both the reused test split and the fresh holdout, so more training variety did not measurably help on images from the sources it trained on. The unseen-source check is descriptive only.
findings.data: Measured: orientation carries class information in some sources. reevald squares and rectangles are 92 to 95% axis-aligned, Quick, Draw! squares 73 to 85%, El Korchi squares are randomly oriented. A0 is a template matcher: its accuracy on rotated validation falls from 93.65 at 0° to 60.9 at 45°, while A1 stays at 89 to 91. The source also gives the class away (source classifier 91.7% against 46.7%).
findings.prep: Measured on validation, three seeds, not on test: A1 with rotation off reached 93.15 macro-F1 and with ±15° reached 93.17, against 91.69 for A0 and 90.03 for A1 with ±180°. Every augmentation and generator range had been set by hand. Two real defects found and fixed: augmented shapes came out about 6 px too small (51 px against 57 px real), and 1-px strokes broke into pieces after warping. The synthetic stroke was 2 px against 3.1 px real. No bug was found in labels or batching.
findings.model: Tuning covered only learning rate and dropout, on A1, and A0 reused A1's winner. A1 is still improving when the 30-epoch budget ends (60 epochs reached 92.11 and 92.38, against 90.44 and 90.71). Early stopping is fragile at learning rate 0.003: validation scores can swing by 30 points between epochs. The loss, polarity and class weighting were checked and are correct. After tuning on validation, mean macro-F1 was A2 95.17, A1 94.77, B 94.20, A0 92.61. Trials per arm: A0 6, A1 30, B 22, A2 18.
findings.eval: Test macro-F1: A0 93.88, A1 90.86, B 90.50. B vs A1 was -0.36, 95% CI [-1.17, 0.41]: fail. Augmentation hurt rectangle, diamond and square and helped octagon and hexagon. On an unseen source the picture reverses: on held-out Hand-Drawn triangles and rectangles (validation) A0 averaged 53.5% accuracy, A1 66.4%, B 71.8%, so A0's lead is specific to sources it trained on. Iteration 2 result: A2 vs A0 is +0.06 points on the reused test split, CI [-0.69, 0.83], and +0.08 on the fresh 4,500-image holdout, CI [-0.41, 0.57]: fail on both. After fixing the transform, every arm reached about the same test macro-F1 (A0 95.3, A1 95.2, B 95.3, A2 95.4). On unseen Hand-Drawn triangles and rectangles, mean accuracy was A0 66.6, A1 74.5, B 72.6, A2 73.8.
findings.deploy: On drawn shapes, A1 and B can call a square a rectangle while A0 is right. That matches the test pattern but is informal evidence only. Iteration 2 exported A2_2 by the validation selection rule (validation macro-F1 95.46), and the studio serves all four arms live. The 60-drawing check is still open.
